text:
mira: RFC-312 follow-up — we need to decide how adapter interfaces should propagate tenant/billing metadata across Hosted / Dedicated / Private. I'm worried about attribution loss when requests fall back to hosted. cc @alex

alex: Good catch. Two vectors: (1) header size/latency if we add lots of fields, (2) trust boundary (hosted vs untrusted private agents). I think minimal wire metadata + a signed provenance token is the right abstraction.

jon: +1 on provenance. Implementation differs by hosting mode though. Dedicated -> internal mTLS means we can trust headers set by controlplane. Private (customer-managed) can't accept arbitrary headers from our controlplane without an agent-side shim.

sara: We already use X-RW-Tenant and X-RW-Auth-Source in some places. The problem: hosted uses bearer tokens, dedicated uses mTLS client cert, private sidecars sometimes strip headers for security. We need a canonical, mode-aware contract.

infra-bot: FYI incident-20240312 showed missing billing labels when fallback to hosted. Root cause: agent stripped org_id header; hosted fallback didn't reconstruct it -> billing gaps. Logs flagged 1.2k requests.

kevin: Proposal: extend adapter interface with AdapterMetadata fields: tenant_id, org_id, route_id, billing_tags[], hop_chain[], provenance_signature (optional). For Private adapters provenance_signature should be required unless the private runtime provides equivalent attestation.

mira: Clarify: provenance_signature = HMAC(header_blob, key)? Who owns the signing key in Private mode? We can't depend on our KMS for on-prem.

alex: Two options: (A) trust-chain hop list (X-RW-Hop) that appends origin info at each hop (lightweight, low crypto) OR (B) per-adapter signatures with keys provisioned at install time. Hop list is easier but weaker for billing guarantees.

jon: Hop list helps tracing/debugging but not authoritative billing. If hosted endpoint is responsible for final billing, it must validate origin. For Dedicated, controlplane-issued certs work. For Private we either provision keys via customer KMS/HSM or accept weaker semantics and mark as 'unverified'.

sara: Decision proposal (for discussion):
- canonical tenant_id accepted only from TrustedBoundary (hosted controlplane or Dedicated controlplane w/ mTLS).
- Private adapters must supply origin_tenant + adapter_attestation (either signature or agent_cert) and server will attempt verification.
- If verification fails, tag request with billing:unknown and route to fallback policy (either reject, soft-rate-limit, or bill to default account per product policy).

mira: Implementation notes: update proto svc/adapter.proto with new message AdapterMeta { map<string,string> tags; repeated string hop_chain; bytes signature; int64 ts }. Also update SDK to populate hop_chain when doing cross-hosting handoffs.

alex: Rollout sketch: 1) add fields but treat optional (opt-in) 2) log mismatches for 2 weeks 3) run canary enforcing verification for a small percentage 4) full enforcement after 4 weeks. @sara can you add this to runbook + migration checklist?

sara: Will do. I'll add telemetry points: percent of requests with missing tenant_id post-fallback, percent with unverified provenance, and a billing-alert if >0.1% of traffic loses attribution. Also add test cases to incident runbook.

kevin: :thumbsup: add unit/integration tests that simulate Private agent stripping headers and verify we label billing:unknown and surface the event to billing pipeline.

mira: One more open item — cache charge semantics. If a response is served from a Dedicated cache but the request fell back to Hosted earlier, who pays? My gut: charge owner of the pinned model/version. If mismatch, escalate to billing-resolution workflow. Needs to be documented in billing RFC.

jon: Agreed. Owner-of-model rule is clean operationally. Add a fallback reconciliation job that reattributes charges when verification later succeeds.

mira: OK I'll draft follow-up RFC (ADL: adapter data layout, verification flows, rollout timeline) and link here. Tagging thread RFC-312-followup. Thanks everyone.

alex: thanks — small action items for next-week: protos PR, runbook entry, telemetry dashboards.

sara: I'll file runbook + dashboard tickets.

infra-bot: Note: created ticket INFRA-8421 for adapter-meta protos.

mira: closing loop — will post RFC draft by EOW.
